verdict_reason: The retraction I was asked to check IS in place -- representation_engineering.py:707-724 now carries 'RETRACTED, 2026-09-06: that note went on to claim "32 draws lands at 2.56 and is stable". It does not.' -- and I verified the shipped default is still 32 (`_N_RAND_DRAWS_DEFAULT = 32`, merged production config {'num_samples': 8, 'steering_alpha': 1.0, 'steering_threshold': 0.01}). BUT THE REPLACEMENT DIAGNOSIS DOES NOT REPRODUCE AND THE TRUTH IS WORSE. First, a fact neither prior review states: the norm-matched random control is seeded on the LAYER INDEX ONLY -- `_g.manual_seed(1234 + 7919 * l_idx)` at repe:1215 -- so the task's `seed` config NEVER reaches it and `steering_concept_over_random` is DETERMINISTIC for a given (model, n_random_draws). I measured that directly: 12 different `seed` values at 8 draws on gpt2 all return 0.7538, sd EXACTLY 0.0000. So the recorded '0.9523 +/- 0.2285 over seeds, CV 24.0%, realizations 0.6357-1.2594' cannot have come from the shipped seed knob, and no 'mean' over seeds exists to drift. Second, increasing n_random_draws EXTENDS the same generator stream, so the draw sequence is one realization's convergence path -- and it does not converge and is not monotone. Measured on gpt2, the shipped deterministic value: 0.766340 (4 draws), 0.753817 (8), 1.201288 (16), 1.052713 (32), 0.704796 (64), 0.801071 (128). That is a 1.70x swing that crosses the 1.0 decision line THREE times, and `steering_beats_random_frac` flips 0.4 -> 0.4 -> 0.6 -> 0.6 -> 0.4 -> 0.4 with it. The shipped 32-draw value says gpt2 BEATS a norm-matched random direction (1.052713); the 64- and 128-draw values on the same weights say it LOSES (0.704796, 0.801071). So the claim of a ~15% monotone high bias (1.0573 -> 0.9523 -> 0.8284) is REFUTED as stated -- the estimator is not biased-but-converging, it is unconverged at 128 draws. I ISOLATED THE MECHANISM by dumping the five per-layer ratios the outer median selects from. gpt2's tested layers are [0, 3, 6, 9, 11] and the NUMERATORS are bit-identical at every draw count ([6.575, -5.664, 100.754, 434.669, 1236.354]); only the random denominators move. Sorted ratios: [0.0, 0.7312, 0.7538, 2.0283, 14.1549] at 8 draws, [0.0, 0.7729, 1.2013, 2.3106, 9.5111] at 16, [0.0, 0.7538, 1.0527, 1.9399, 9.8223] at 32, [0.0, 0.6727, 0.7048, 1.7581, 8.9864] at 64. The reported headline is the 3rd of those five, and WHICH LAYER occupies that rank changes: layer 6 at 8 draws, LAYER 0 at 16 and 32, layer 6 again at 64. Layer 0 has by far the smallest denominator (5.473-9.774 against 87-247 elsewhere) and therefore the noisiest ratio (0.6727-1.2013, a 1.79x swing), and it is precisely that ratio that crosses the middle rank. Worse, layer 3 contributes EXACTLY 0.0 at every draw count -- `max(0.0, dir_pos[l])` clamps its negative effect (-5.664) to zero -- so one of the five order statistics is a structural constant and the 'median of 5' is really the 2nd smallest of the four non-zero ratios. This is not Monte Carlo noise that more draws will average away; it is a rank statistic over five numbers, one of which is pinned at 0 and another of which is dominated by the smallest denominator in the set. YELLOW rather than RED because the estimand itself is a declared BLME proxy (task_metadata: 'proxy-only'; the hook is verified against the official RepE `linear_comb` at token_pos='end') and the code's own comment already tells a reader the number is unreliable; but the specific disclosure now on the file is the wrong description of the problem, and leaving the default at 32 with THAT disclosure is not defensible when the neighbouring draw counts invert the conclusion.
comparable_reason: The layer set is a DEPTH-CLASS DISCONTINUITY, not a smooth function of depth: repe:1084-1088 tests `[0, L//4, L//2, 3L//4, L-1]` when L > 10 and `range(L)` otherwise. So gpt2 (12 layers) and gpt2-medium (24) are each summarised over 5 sampled layers while distilgpt2 and pythia-70m (6 layers) are summarised over ALL 6 -- a different estimator on either side of L = 10, applied to the same key name. On top of that the headline is the median of only 5 (or 6) per-layer ratios, so a single layer moving across the middle rank changes the reported number discontinuously, which is exactly what the draw sweep shows within a single model. And the reported value cannot be compared to itself across runs at different n_random_draws (1.70x swing over 4..128 draws on identical weights), let alone across models.
normalized_variant: steering_concept_over_random (the ratio to a norm-matched random direction IS the normalisation)
github_reason: The steering hook is a port of RepE's `linear_comb` at token_pos='end' and task_metadata records the head-to-head (per-layer KL == fp64 reference <= 1.7e-6; alpha = 0 -> KL ~ 0). I did not re-run that comparison this round; what I verified against the SOURCE was the control's own construction. The summary the task is read on -- `steering_concept_over_random`, `steering_beats_random_frac`, `directional_consistency`, `directional_success_rate` -- is explicitly BLME's own and has no reference implementation, which task_metadata states ('KL effectiveness/success-rate summary is BLME's own'; verified_d, 'proxy-only, NOT externally verifiable by design').
paper_reason: Zou et al. 2023 and Turner et al. 2023 (ActAdd) report steering successes qualitatively and via task-specific accuracies on their own prompt sets; neither publishes a 'concept effect over norm-matched random direction' ratio for a base LM on a bundled 8-triple probe set, so there is no like-for-like scalar. The reproducible anchors are internal and are the ones task_metadata names: alpha = 0 must give KL ~ 0, and the sign control must satisfy dir(-v) = -dir(+v). The live production run I drove returns steering_sign_reversal 0.832027427531845 (the directional control, ~1 expected in the linear regime) against `_meta_kl_sign_reversal` 0.032073747877463726 (KL, ~0 expected), which is the right qualitative separation.
confounds_reason: Not measurable as a clean correlation on this metric, because the estimator changes form at L = 10 (5 sampled layers above, all layers below) -- so any cross-model correlation with n_layers is partly a change of estimator rather than a property of the models. That discontinuity is itself an architecture dependence. The ratio construction does remove the obvious width channel: the denominator is a norm-MATCHED random direction, so the task-vector norm (which grows with d_model) cancels to first order. Recorded as SUSPECTED rather than CONFIRMED because the run-to-run instability within a single model (1.70x over draw counts) exceeds any between-model signal I could measure, which makes a confound test uninformative until the estimator is stabilised.
defects: CODE, representation_engineering.py:1427 + 1084-1088: `steering_concept_over_random` is the MEDIAN of a per-layer ratio over exactly 5 tested layers (for L > 10), so the headline is a rank statistic that does not converge in n_random_draws. Measured on gpt2 at the shipped config: 0.766340 / 0.753817 / 1.201288 / 1.052713 / 0.704796 / 0.801071 at 4 / 8 / 16 / 32 / 64 / 128 draws -- a 1.70x range crossing the 1.0 decision line three times, with `steering_beats_random_frac` flipping 0.4/0.4/0.6/0.6/0.4/0.4. The shipped 32-draw answer ('beats random', 1.052713) is contradicted by the 64- and 128-draw answers on identical weights (0.704796, 0.801071). Isolated per layer: the numerators are bit-identical across draw counts ([6.575, -5.664, 100.754, 434.669, 1236.354] at layers [0, 3, 6, 9, 11]) and the sorted ratios are [0.0, 0.7312, 0.7538, 2.0283, 14.1549] / [0.0, 0.7729, 1.2013, 2.3106, 9.5111] / [0.0, 0.7538, 1.0527, 1.9399, 9.8223] / [0.0, 0.6727, 0.7048, 1.7581, 8.9864] at 8/16/32/64 draws, so the middle rank changes hands between layer 6 and layer 0. Layer 0's denominator is 5.473-9.774 against 87-247 for the others, making its ratio the least stable member and the one that decides the headline.

CODE, representation_engineering.py:1427: `_ratios = [max(0.0, dir_pos[l]) / abs(dir_rand[l]) ...]` clamps a layer that steers AGAINST its own concept to exactly 0.0. The clamp is right on its own terms (that layer should not score a large positive), but it is applied INSIDE a 5-point median: on gpt2 layer 3 has effect -5.664 and contributes exactly 0.0 at every draw count, so one of the five order statistics is a structural constant and the 'median of 5' is in practice the 2nd smallest of the four non-zero ratios. Any model with two wrong-way layers would have the median pinned at or near 0 regardless of the other three.

CODE, representation_engineering.py:1215: `_g.manual_seed(1234 + 7919 * l_idx)` hard-codes the control-RNG base and keys it only on the layer index, so the task's `seed` config does not reach the random control at all. Verified: 12 distinct `seed` values at 8 draws give 0.7538 with sd EXACTLY 0.0000, matching the deterministic 0.753817. Consequence for the campaign: any recorded 'seed-to-seed spread' for this metric (including '0.9523 +/- 0.2285, CV 24.0%, realizations 0.6357-1.2594') did not come from this knob and cannot be reproduced through it, and there is no way for a user to estimate the control's own sampling error without editing the source.

DISCLOSURE IS NOW WRONG IN A NEW WAY, representation_engineering.py:707-724: the retraction correctly withdraws '32 draws lands at 2.56 and is stable', but replaces it with 'the MEAN drifts monotonically 1.0573 -> 0.9523 -> 0.8284 over the same counts, so the shipped 32-draw value is about 15% biased HIGH'. Measured, the sequence is neither monotone nor a mean over anything (there is no seed variation to average), and the 32-draw value is the LOCAL MAXIMUM of my 4..128 sweep, not 15% above a converging limit. A reader acting on the current comment would subtract ~15% from 1.052713 and get 0.895, when the 64-draw value is 0.704796.
COMPARABILITY, repe:1084-1088: `test_layers` is 5 sampled layers for L > 10 and every layer for L <= 10, so the same key name is two different estimators on either side of a hard depth cut.

CONFIG (correct, and worth keeping), tasks.yaml:172: num_samples = 8 now matches the bundled probe set exactly, and the live run confirms it -- `_meta_n_probe_triples` = 8, `_meta_probe_set_is_bundled` = true. The earlier 3-triple window dependence is closed.
fix: Two changes, in order of importance. (1) Replace the outer MEDIAN over 5 layers with a quantity that converges: report the mean of the per-layer ratios (or, better, the ratio of the pooled numerator to the pooled denominator) so more draws tighten the estimate instead of relabelling which layer sits in the middle; keep the median under `_meta_steering_concept_over_random_median` so archived values stay recoverable. Until that is done, raising n_random_draws does not fix the number and the disclosure should say so. (2) Seed the control generator from the task config -- `_g.manual_seed(int(self.config.get('seed', 42)) * 1000003 + 7919 * l_idx)` -- so the control's sampling error is measurable through the shipped knob, and emit the per-layer ratio spread as `_meta_steering_ratio_layer_spread` so a reader can see that the headline rests on a 5-point median. Also correct the retraction at repe:707-724 to describe non-convergence rather than a monotone 15% bias, quoting the 4..128 sequence.
